$comment: Curated state and regional records. Each value that matters carries a verbatim quote from the official program page it was read from, with the retrieval date. The curated adapter re-checks each quote during ingestion; a missing quote queues the record for review. This is production data, not a fixture.

records.name: Driving Clean Assistance Program (DCAP) - Clean Cars 4 All pathway
records.providerName: California Air Resources Board (Driving Clean Assistance Program)
records.summary: Statewide CARB-funded scrap-and-replace grant for income-qualified Californians: up to $10,000 (up to $12,000 in designated Disadvantaged Communities) toward a new or used battery electric vehicle, plus $2,000 toward Level 2 home charging or a $2,000 prepaid public-charging card. Residents of air districts that run their own Clean Cars 4 All program must use that program instead.

evidence.quote: are eligible for up to $12,000 for these vehicles.

amounts.label: Up to $10,000 for a new or used BEV

evidence.quote: up to $10,000 to purchase or lease a new or used battery electric vehicle
$2,000 towards the purchase and installation of level 2 home charging equipment.
A $2,000 prepaid charge card to pay for public charging.

records.stackingNote: Each program's own rules decide whether it can be combined with other state, local or utility incentives; ClearEV does not add amounts together.

coverage.note: California residents; the page states residents of an air district with its own CC4A program are not eligible to scrap and replace through DCAP.

summary: Household income less than 300% of the Federal Poverty Level (page notes the threshold is subject to change every year).
Must be a California resident (AB60 and ITIN holders qualify).
Residents of an air district with its own Clean Cars 4 All program are not eligible for DCAP scrap-and-replace.

Vehicle to retire: gasoline or diesel light- or medium-duty vehicle under 10,000 lbs GVWR that passes a functionality test, with two years' proof of operation; the page lists model year 2010 or older for 2025 applications.

Replacement vehicle: new or used, bought or leased from an authorized California dealership, purchase price cap $45,000; used vehicles must be 8 calendar years or newer with 75,000 or fewer original miles.

vehicle.maxPriceNote: Maximum purchase price cap of $45,000, excluding taxes and fees.

evidence.quote: New or used with a maximum purchase price cap of $45,000 (excluding taxes and fees).

restrictions: Must scrap a qualifying older vehicle.
The separate DCAP Financing Assistance pathway is closed to new applications.

steps: Check eligibility on the DCAP eligibility page.
Apply online through the DCAP application portal.
Once approved, buy or lease an eligible vehicle from an authorized California dealership and retire the old vehicle through the program.
documents: Two years' proof of operation for the vehicle being retired
application.deadlineNote: No end date stated on the page.

records.statusBasis: The DCAP home page states the Clean Cars 4 All pathway is open and accepting applications; only the Financing Assistance pathway is closed.

statusEvidence.quote: Clean Cars 4 All, is still open and accepting applications from all tiers.

records.verificationMethod: Read from the official program page and quoted verbatim; quotes are re-checked against the page on each ingestion run.
uncertainties: Eligibility page states the retired-vehicle model-year rule for calendar year 2025 applications; the 2026 rule is not stated.
Which air districts count as having their own CC4A program is not listed on the eligibility page (CARB says five participating districts).
Remaining funding level not stated.
